answer: Think of a reputation score as a lotus pond: each genuine agent earns petals by completing verified tasks over time, while fake accounts stay as bare seeds that cannot bloom. Peers watch the crystal-clear ledger where these petals accumulate, and a new identity trying to impersonate others arrives carrying only an unlit lantern - no history, no earned trust - so the network quietly dims its access until it either disappears or does real, provable work to earn light.
